2.stem: The writer wants to explain why the researchers conducted the second experiment. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: In the first experiment, plants supplied with extra CO2 grew 30% taller than they otherwise would have, a difference large enough to demand an explanation.
options.B: They conducted the second experiment to rule out the possibility that heat from the apparatus, rather than the CO2, was causing the extra growth.
options.C: Plants in the second experiment, which ran the same apparatus on normal air at the identical temperature, showed no extra growth at all over the whole trial.
options.D: Taken together, the two experiments confirmed that it was the CO2 and not the temperature of the apparatus that was responsible for the extra growth.

3.stem: The student wants to generalize the pattern in a way a skeptical reader would accept. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: The one vent that lacked these bacteria turned out to have unusually low sulfide, the very compound on which the bacteria depend for the energy they supply to the food web.
options.B: Researchers sampled the microbial mats growing at twelve separate hydrothermal vents in the course of the study.
options.C: These chemosynthetic bacteria form the base of the food web at the vents, supporting the tube worms and the other animals that crowd around the openings in the sea floor.
options.D: Sulfide-using bacteria appeared at 11 of the 12 vents sampled, and across three different oceans, indicating they are a widespread foundation of vent ecosystems.

7.stem: The student wants to convey to a general reader why this innovation matters. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: The new stabilizer is a sugar-based gel, and a vaccine mixed with it stays viable for six months at room temperature instead of having to be kept frozen at -20°C.
options.B: By keeping the vaccine stable at room temperature, the stabilizer could bring it to the roughly two-thirds of the world where reliable freezing is unavailable.
options.C: Keeping a vaccine frozen at -20°C requires costly equipment and an electricity supply that does not fail, which is what led the researchers to look for a stabilizer.
options.D: Normally the vaccine must be kept frozen at -20°C, a temperature that no ordinary refrigerator can reach and that many clinic freezers cannot hold steadily for long.

8.stem: The student wants to generalize the finding in a way a skeptical reader—wary of sweeping claims—would accept. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: The self-healing mineral aluminous tobermorite forms when seawater reacts with the volcanic ash in the concrete, filling cracks in the harbor structures as they open.
options.B: Unlike Roman concrete, which was mixed with volcanic ash, modern Portland cement contains none and shows no comparable mineral growth sealing the cracks that open in it.
options.C: In 9 of the 10 marine structures sampled, the concrete showed self-healing mineral growth, indicating the effect is characteristic of Roman seawater concrete.
options.D: Because the only sample without self-healing growth came from a freshwater river site, seawater must be what triggers the effect in every structure the Romans ever built.

9.stem: The student wants to offer a cautious generalization that a skeptical reader would be likely to accept. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Across several studies, remote work was associated with modest productivity gains in some settings, though the effects varied by job type.
options.B: A 2023 study of two firms found no significant difference between remote and in-office workers, so the gains reported in the other studies are unlikely to be real.
options.C: Remote work makes employees more productive, as studies of four tech firms and of a call center have now established beyond reasonable dispute for any job.
options.D: A 2021 study of a call center found that remote workers handled 13% more calls than their in-office peers, a gain that can be expected to hold across most job types.

10.stem: The student wants to emphasize how photography became progressively more accessible to ordinary people over time. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Successive innovations steadily lowered the skill and equipment demands of photography, until roll film in 1888 finally put cameras in amateurs' hands.
options.B: The wet collodion process of the 1850s shortened exposure times to only a few seconds.
options.C: Early daguerreotypes of the 1840s required subjects to hold still for several minutes.
options.D: Dry gelatin plates, introduced in the 1870s, could be manufactured in advance and stored.

11.stem: The student wants to emphasize, for a general reader, why the discovery is significant. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Recovering and sequencing the ancient genetic material took the research team eight years of work, from the first attempts on the tooth to the finished sequence.
options.B: The genetic material the team analyzed was recovered from the tooth of a single mammoth, an animal that lived roughly 1.2 million years ago and left the tooth behind.
options.C: Until this study, the oldest genetic material that anyone had ever managed to recover was roughly 700,000 years old, a record that had stood for a long time.
options.D: By recovering the oldest DNA ever found, more than doubling the previous record, the study opens the door to reading the genes of other ancient creatures.

17.stem: The student wants to convey why antibiotic resistance is a serious concern. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Antibiotic-resistant infections already cause an estimated 1.3 million deaths a year, and once-simple infections could again become deadly.
options.B: Overuse of antibiotics in farming, where whole herds of healthy livestock are dosed routinely as a precaution, accelerates the spread of resistant bacteria.
options.C: Certain strains of bacteria have evolved resistance to the antibiotics that doctors have prescribed most commonly for decades.
options.D: Few new classes of antibiotics have been developed since the 1980s, and most drugs in use today were introduced before then.

18.stem: The student wants to present a cautious summary of the findings. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Herrera's findings suggest the hoods helped but did not solve the problem: across the 9 bakeries sampled, average dust fell by roughly 38 percent, yet levels during hand bench dusting still exceeded the recommended limit.
options.B: Herrera's findings suggest the hoods helped but did not solve the problem: across the 12 bakeries sampled, average dust fell by roughly 51 percent, yet levels during dough sheeting runs still exceeded the recommended limit.
options.C: Herrera's findings suggest the hoods helped but did not solve the problem: across the 15 bakeries sampled, average dust fell by roughly 64 percent, yet levels during end-of-day sweeping still exceeded the recommended limit.
options.D: Herrera's findings suggest the hoods helped but did not solve the problem: across the 6 bakeries sampled, average dust fell by roughly 22 percent, yet levels during flour sack emptying still exceeded the recommended limit.

19.stem: The student wants to introduce the study's central finding to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Of the 200 blackpoll warblers fitted with geolocators in 2013, only 5 came back carrying data the researchers could use.
options.B: In 2013 researchers fitted 200 blackpoll warblers with geolocators light enough not to burden a bird of about 12 grams, then waited for the birds to return the following year.
options.C: Before the 2013 study appeared, scientists had long debated whether songbirds as small as blackpoll warblers could cross open ocean.
options.D: A 2013 study of blackpoll warblers—songbirds weighing just 12 grams—found that they fly nonstop across the Atlantic, up to 2,700 km, over as long as three days.

21.stem: The student wants to emphasize the sequence of warning signs that preceded the eruption. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: In the weeks before the March 12 eruption, the warning signs mounted in order: first earthquakes, then ground bulging, then a spike in sulfur gas.
options.B: Sulfur gas emissions spiked in the hours before the eruption, rising far above the levels the monitoring station had recorded in any earlier month of that year.
options.C: The volcano erupted on March 12, and the eruption is now among the most closely documented events of its kind anywhere in the region's recent history.
options.D: Scientists now use signals like these as eruption warnings, which is why monitoring instruments are installed on volcanoes that have been quiet for decades.

22.stem: The student wants to acknowledge a limitation of the study. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Ontiveros's conclusion that longer soaks cut glaze defects is limited: the logs were filled in by volunteer members rather than by automated controllers and never recorded the age or condition of each kiln.
options.B: Ontiveros's conclusion that longer soaks cut glaze defects is limited: the logs covered only firings from November through February and never recorded the thickness of the glaze application.
options.C: Ontiveros's conclusion that longer soaks cut glaze defects is limited: the logs came only from studios that fire with electric kilns and never recorded the clay body used in each firing.
options.D: Ontiveros's conclusion that longer soaks cut glaze defects is limited: the logs came from four studios in a single city and never recorded how tightly each kiln was loaded.

23.stem: The student wants to acknowledge a limitation of the study. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Nandakumar found that 78 percent of waiting riders stood inside a shelter, but her observations were limited to the months of June, July, and August, so the figure cannot be taken as a village-wide measure.
options.B: Nandakumar found that 55 percent of waiting riders stood inside a shelter, but her observations were limited to the two shelters on Ashcombe's paved main roads, so the figure cannot be taken as a village-wide measure.
options.C: Nandakumar found that 62 percent of waiting riders stood inside a shelter, but her observations were limited to the three shelters nearest the village center, so the figure cannot be taken as a village-wide measure.
options.D: Nandakumar found that 41 percent of waiting riders stood inside a shelter, but her observations were limited to weekday mornings between 7 and 9 a.m., so the figure cannot be taken as a village-wide measure.
